Chunk 2 line 13: 'M2 used this without naming it: **find is easier than judge**' — 'this' resolves to the cheap/expensive-check heuristic stated in lines 11-12, same chunk; 'the map' in the same bullet is arc-earned spine vocabulary (this rule's own carve-out example is literally 'the map'), not a fresh unexplained referent. Chunk 3 line 17-19 (edited since pin e11bbeb4: bullet now reads 'No cheap verifier? Keep the task, or build the verifier first and then delegate.', the fragment 'Two options.' was cut): 'trap' at line 19 reuses 'a trap' named at chunk 2 line 12, and 'delegation-trap to delegation-win' at line 19 reuses both halves of that same coinage — a term introduced on an earlier slide and reused, explicitly a NOT-violation. The edit itself introduces no new referent to resolve; 'the task' and 'the verifier' in the shortened bullet are the chunk's own header nouns. No never-named, vague, or stranded referents anywhere in the deck.

Chunk 2 line 13: 'M2 used this without naming it: **find is easier than judge**' names the source by module and unpacks the claim in the same sentence — the rule's preferred form, not a positional pointer ('the opening lecture said'). Maintainer STATUS paragraph (line 27, unchanged since pin) documents this as cleared, deliberate lineage-naming: 'already enacted in M2 body as "find is easier than judge"... the body's M2 back-reference is deliberate lineage-naming, kept per the audit's cheap-groundedness call... the ref is backward-naming of a lived moment, not sequencing.' No cross-file positional violation.

Each of the 3 content chunks carries 3 substantial, self-carrying bullets (lines 5-7, 11-13, 17-19) — none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent fragment; the shortened line-18 bullet still carries a full claim (name the cheap verifier or build one before delegating). Chunk 0 is the standard title-only H1 lede, not a content orphan.

'Checking can cost far less than doing' (line 3) is delivered by lines 5-7. 'Why this decides what to delegate' (line 9) is delivered by lines 11-13 — closest-to-violating case since it is phrased as 'why' rather than a flat assertion, but the content directly cashes out the implied claim, so it stays inside. 'Every send-off needs a named cheap verifier' (line 15) is delivered by lines 17-19, including the shortened line 18 — the trimmed wording still names the verifier question the header promises. No header the chunk's own content contradicts.

Read all 9 body bullets against each sub-item, including the edited line 18. No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction (the deleted fragment 'Two options.' was itself a candidate list-preamble, not a banned triad, and its removal only tightens the bullet). No anaphora/epistrophe triples anywhere. No self-grading superlatives (line 18's 'more valuable half of the work' is generic verifier-authoring advice about the reader's future work, not self-praise of this page or training). No number-plus-retraction hedging — body carries no numeric claims (dated_line grep: 0 hits, planted-proof CLEAN). No abstraction-noun stacks — 'delegation-trap to delegation-win' (line 19) and 'the full cost comes back to you at read time' (line 12) name concrete consequences. No verb triplets with an empty leg. Closest-to-violating: line 19 echoes line 12's 'trap' but adds a new claim (task-family conversion), so it stays inside.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This page is lecture-shaped doctrine (a 'Laws carried' page per its own maintainer block), not an exercise, so the claim standard applies. Two of three headings are flat declarative claims: 'Checking can cost far less than doing' (line 3), 'Every send-off needs a named cheap verifier' (line 15). The third, 'Why this decides what to delegate' (line 9), is the closest-to-violating case — phrased as a 'why' frame rather than a bald assertion like the rule's own examples — but stays inside because 'this decides what to delegate' is itself a compressed causal claim (the asymmetry determines the delegate/keep decision), not a topic label. No imperative task-instruction headings anywhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all 9 bullets against the three classes, with particular attention to the edited line 18 since a trim is exactly where a bullet can collapse into a restatement. (a) doctrine restatement: none — the edit ('No cheap verifier? Keep the task, or build the verifier first and then delegate.') still adds two distinct options not stated elsewhere (keep vs. build-then-delegate), it does not re-announce a split already landed. Closest case remains chunk 2 line 13 ('M2 used this without naming it... it runs through the whole far half of the map'), which stays inside because it adds a new fact (this M2 law IS an instance of the asymmetry) plus a scope claim. (b) self-referential design commentary: none. (c) aphorism kicker: closest case is chunk 3 line 19 ('Every verifier you write converts one more task family from delegation-trap to delegation-win. That is why checks are worth authoring at all.') — stays inside because it elevates the prior bullet's single-task framing to a task-family-level justification, a new priority claim, not a koan restating the header (no **The point:** line exists in this file to restate).
